I really enjoy Phantom Brave. This is a remake of the PS2 version, and while it seems simple at first, it can become extremely detailed through 'failure fusions', collecting dungeon boss items, and combining skills.

It is similar to the Disgaea franchise, but the movement system feels much more natural to me (even slippery ground). Instead of moving on specific squares, you can move freely within a set range. The speed stat also matters a lot, since it can let you act multiple times before an enemy gets a turn.

The best part is the story, (its a feel good story)

The worst part, for me, is that dungeons do not show the total number of floors while you are inside them. For example, if you are on floor 39 of 45, the game only says “floor 39” instead of '39/45'

Overall, I would recommend it to fans of strategy RPGs, especially people who like Disgaea but want a different kind of movement system and a stronger focus on story.

Game is fire. True disgea fans know this is THE game after the first disgea. Game is grindy. I remember getting to lvl 7000 on the psp but I honestly got no idea how I did that after replaying it. Still game is very strategy based.

Here are some hints for beginners. Use the starfish weapon. The green ghost npc clearly states speed is king. The starfish provides an aoe as its basic attack. All its attacks are based on speed, and it has long range skills that hit hard. Make a map with fish and steal a lvl 20 starfish or a couple. This might require a few resets. After this lvl up the starfish and when you reach its level(20) you hunt for a lvl 40 starfish. Rinse and repeat. After you get to lvl 80 or 100 using the strategy the game starts to open up. Always aim to steal weapons 40 levels higher and dont get attached to low lvl weapons. You can use any npc you like even monsters since they can hold weapons. Affinity to elements is extremely important. Always abuse elements it can make the difference between double damage or 0. Starfish is great because it trains you the red thunder sigil. Which can be used with special or physical attacks. The starfish makes your HP hit 1 point so becareful with this. It essentially makes you into a glass cannon. Ash should never hold the starfish but a sword. 

Another hint is that the beginner box skills are OP. AOE straight line with low cost and fire element. Fuse it with the starfish as the secondary weapon and make the starfish learn its skills. 

All attacks are based on a stat. Dont ignore those. The best stat is speed and second is HP. 

The game is deep and you start seeing new things as you go deeper and you also unlock certain characters that cant be unlocked at novice levels. 

The story is great and its voice acting is superb. 

Titles are also very important. Attaching and growing titles will make your weapons OP and this is how you train new characters, Give your OP weapons to lvl 1 characters to train them. 

In battle prioritize enemies that like to steal. If they steal your OP weapon then gg. Ill update at a later time with a more thorough review. Honestly if youre able to make it to lvl 100 you can make it to lvl 9999. Games mechanics are pretty straight forward.

Edit: I realized I was playing the game the wrong way this whole time. Failure fusion is the way to go. I did manage to beat the final boss without it but damn that was tough. It was a good experience. I wouldnt recommend it since it took me 100 hours for that. Now to the extra stages

[h1][b] TLDR: A heartwarming story and unique mechanics, but the gameplay just wasn’t fun to me. [/b] [/h1]

[h1]PROS: [/h1]
➕Creative spirit binding mechanics
➕Quality port - 120 FPS, HD text/UI
➕Marona is adorable

[h1]CONS: [/h1]
➖Can’t exit battles once inside them, only reload
➖Attacking the right target can be difficult with free-form selection
➖Many confusing/not well explained mechanics
➖Characters going away after a set number of turns (Remove) can get annoying

You can see my other reviews for NIS here (in release order): 
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/Synikx/recommended/1866420?snr=1_5_9__402]La Pucelle: Ragnarok[/url]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/Synikx/recommended/405900?snr=1_5_9__402]Disgaea[/url]


[h1] [b] Content (Game world/Narrative) – [4/10] [/b] [/h1]
The game world takes elements from La Pucelle and Disgaea - You have a world map with all of the different stages on it, similar to La Pucelle. The battle maps are more like Disgaea with things like throwing and Geo Symbol-type mechanics being present. 
I found the world to be a step up from both La Pucelle and Disgaea, I think the creativity of the mechanics blend really well with the items in the zones. 

The narrative is more like La Pucelle than Disgaea. This is a serious story full of moments that tug on your heart. Marona, the protagonist, is an adorable, but naive little girl (voiced by Flonne from Disgaea!). She is what’s called a “Chroma”, which is a person that communicates with spirits. Marona herself is known as “The cursed girl” and is often treated horribly. Marona is pretty much a doormat for most of the game as she gets walked all over constantly by NPCs that take advantage of her. 
I didn’t enjoy the narrative, it wasn’t good enough to keep me interested to finish. I would say it’s about the same as La Pucelle from the tone, but it doesn’t have as many interesting hooks as Disgaea. 

[h1][b] Gameplay (Mechanics/Difficulty) – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
The mechanics are unique here. Note that unique does not necessarily mean good. I found the mechanics to be cumbersome, vague/not explained well, and in general not fun. But, on the other hand, they are so unique that I wanted to keep playing to explore it more, unfortunately, all the disadvantages kept piling up. I struggle to think of a mechanic that doesn’t come with a downside that makes me dislike it. 

-Marona is kind of plays like a necromancer, it adds strategic elements to play around characters removing after a set time….but this also means that the player not only experiences detachment from their characters, but it almost seems pointless to focus power on anyone other than Marona, since she is the only character that stays around permanently.

-The title/fusion/blacksmith mechanics are interesting, it plays well thematically by removing the grind burden from characters and putting them on items…but I found this system to be very confusing, and the game does a poor job at explaining it. Even after reading guides, I didn’t like how I had to grind failure titles over and over to use on weapons and maps. This is not as exciting or interesting as Disgaea’s “Innocent” system. 

-The grid movement system of La Pucelle and Disgaea are replaced with a free-form movement and targeting system. This is cool with the available freedom….but choosing a specific target can get challenging when there are multiple NPCs near each other. Also, the grid system limited the amount of targets that can attack (one on each side), not so here. Being surrounded and attacked by enemies is a real possibility, and while you can do the same, you are restricted by the removal of your characters, unlike the enemy. 

I would say this is a fairly difficult game. Aside from the issues by there being a forced time limit on your characters, the beginning is challenging due to lack of resources. I found myself pretty much breaking even after every mission by having to heal my characters. This means I couldn’t spend that much money on getting items or creating new characters (which are a pain to level fresh…). You can’t even engage in systems like random dungeons without spending money. I feel like the burden is way too much at the start. 

[h1] [b] Graphics (Quality/Technical) – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
Pretty good. The sprites/backgrounds are clearly the original and very pixelated. The UI is crisp and high quality. This could pass as a PS3-era title, with the improvements in quality. Still, not very impressive overall since this is a 2004 title, only so much can be done graphically. I feel like this is a step up from Disgaea, though. 

On the technical side, I found no bugs outside the frequent issues with free-form movement. The game behaves well in the background and I had no issues with tabbing or crashes.

[h1] [b] Audio – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
The audio is okay. I didn’t find it as good as Disgaea as far as memorable songs go. 

There is ample voice acting and it is done well. All NIS games seem to have great English voice acting. 

[h1] [b] Replay Factor (Longevity) – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
Tough to say, as most NIS games have a lot of replay value through grinding. I would say the opportunity is there if you can wrestle enough with the title/fusion system. 

[h1] [b] Final Verdict – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
I first played Phantom Brave (PB) waay back on its release in 2004 on the PS2. I remember that I loved Disgaea so much that I saw this game release from the same developer, so I wanted to check it out. Furthermore, I remember that even back then I didn’t enjoy it much and didn’t finish it. Now, free from teenage angst, I wanted to give it another go to see if I could finish it. 

When I first played it, I hated the story so much that I dropped it. I didn’t like how cutesy it was and was expecting something more like Disgaea. This time when I played it, I can accept the story, though it’s not as good as Disgaea, it’s not a dealbreaker. This time, though, it’s the mechanics that have soured the experience for me. You can read more above in the mechanics section for specifics, but to summarize, I simply wasn’t having fun, as such, I cannot give a recommendation to this game. 

Instead of PB, I suggest checking out Disgaea. I’ve only played the first one so far, but it’s a spectacular game. 

[h1] [b] Recommend? (Price) [Y/N] [/b] [/h1]
[h1]No[/h1]
$20 base is a bit steep for a game from 2004. Historical data shows the price on Steam goes as low as $3, which I would recommend it at that price.

A remake of a 2004 PS2 title, this one has considerable bugs and an extremely grindy nature.

Graphically it looks strange, with very pixelated sprite-like character models, and far more detailed non-pixelated backgrounds.  Music's great, sound effects are solid.

Gameplay is a fairly standard strategy RPG, but there's no grid.  Each chapter, and even some story steps, greatly increases the enemy damage, scaling, and more importantly speed.  This necessitates making a randomized dungeon to grind with, both for XP and money, and for items to hopefully take back to your camp that have good titles.  Those titles affect your stats and the stat bonuses of the weapons you equip, so it's very important to get them as soon as possible.  This leads to sometimes an hour grind in a randomized dungeon just to get enough speed and power to deal with the next story mission.  If you like old RPG grinding you may not mind it, but with the below bugs I simply didn't have the drive to continue on.  It's unfortunate too since I was liking the story and gameplay.  In addition, most of your early game units are absolutely terrible, their speed is just too bad to be viable, yet you need to use them enough to get some speedier classes unlocked (such as valkyries or witches) and it can take a while to grind out the resources needed to buy them.  Money is in very short supply through a lot of the early game, adding to the grind.

There are lots of bugs.  One of the biggest and most annoying is that if you tab out for any reason, then when you tab in the game either crashes or completely freezes.  I never found a solution to this issue.  Since it's gridless, enemies and players can move onto or even stand on top of other objects (including enemies!).  When this happens it's difficult or sometimes even impossible to target whatever's on there.  Since your characters can be hit with friendly fire, and characters are only active for a limited amount of time before they de-summon (and cannot be summoned for the rest of the battle), this can cause you to lose runs as you just can't target a foe in any way (ie if the character the enemy is standing on just had their turn and now can't move to force the enemy off).  Some maps (usually ones marked slippery) can have your characters teleport to other spots on the map or even got knocked out of bounds completely with no way to get them back.  Whether this is part of the "slippery" terrain type or a bug I'm unsure, but either way it's frustrating to now no longer be able to reach your target, or have your movement plans messed up.

I was liking the story, Marona is an adorable protagonist, and some of the game design features are really fun and creative; but the high grind factor and high number of bugs makes it no longer worth my time.

Phantom Brave PC is a tactical RPG built around free-movement positioning rather than grid-based strategy, giving every battle a more fluid and improvisational feel. Characters can move anywhere within their range and push or throw objects and enemies, which creates a system where the terrain matters as much as raw stats. This freedom allows for clever tactics but also introduces a level of chaos that defines the game’s identity.

The core mechanic revolves around Marona, a young girl who summons phantom allies by “confining” them to objects on the battlefield. Each object affects the summoned unit’s stats, encouraging experimentation with different combinations. Because phantoms can only stay active for a limited number of turns, the player must plan deployments carefully instead of relying on static party formation.

Marona’s story is unusually heartfelt for a strategy RPG. It follows her effort to help people despite constant mistrust and isolation caused by her powers. The narrative focuses heavily on empathy, selflessness, and emotional resilience, giving the game a softer tone compared to other titles from Nippon Ichi Software.

Progression is built around deep customization. Units can be strengthened through fusion, item enhancement, and leveling systems that offer extreme flexibility. This depth allows for highly optimized builds but can also feel overwhelming to newcomers due to the amount of micromanagement available.

Battlefields are diverse and include environmental quirks such as slippery tiles, stat-altering zones, and movable objects. Combined with the free-movement system, these elements encourage creative solutions rather than straightforward trading of attacks. Fights often turn into puzzles where positioning and turn limits matter more than brute force.

The PC version includes improved performance, higher resolutions, and all previously released content, making it the most complete edition of the game. While the visuals reflect its early-2000s origins, the art direction remains charming, and the soundtrack contributes significantly to the game’s emotional tone.

Phantom Brave PC stands out as a flexible, inventive strategy RPG that rewards creativity and long-term planning. Its combination of free-form battles, robust customization, and a surprisingly earnest story makes it a distinctive experience within the genre, especially for players who enjoy unconventional tactical mechanics.

Phantom Brave PC, developed by Nippon Ichi Software and PH3 GmbH and published by NIS America, is a tactical role-playing game that brings a unique and imaginative approach to the genre. Originally released for the PlayStation 2 in 2004, this PC edition, released in 2016, updates the classic with enhanced visuals and additional content drawn from the PSP port Phantom Brave: Hermuda Triangle. The game stands out in the crowded tactical RPG landscape with its innovative mechanics, whimsical narrative, and deep customization options, offering both longtime fans and new players an engaging strategic experience.

The story of Phantom Brave PC follows Marona, a young girl with the extraordinary ability to see and communicate with phantoms, and her loyal companion, Ash. Together, they undertake missions across a fantastical world where humans and spirits coexist. The narrative balances lighthearted humor with moments of genuine emotional depth, presenting a cast of memorable characters and charming interactions. While the plot may not reinvent storytelling in RPGs, it provides a strong, heartfelt framework that motivates players to engage with the game’s battles and exploration, and it is enriched by quirky side quests and character-driven narratives that reward attentive play.

The game’s combat system is a standout feature, eschewing traditional grid-based movement for a fully gridless tactical environment. This freedom of movement allows for nuanced positioning, creative strategies, and more dynamic encounters. One of the most distinctive mechanics is the ability to bind phantoms to objects in the environment—such as flowers, rocks, or other items—granting them unique abilities and altering their stats. This system encourages experimentation, as players must carefully consider which objects to use and how to best leverage their phantoms’ strengths. Coupled with an extensive customization system, including weapon upgrades, skills, and class development, the game offers considerable strategic depth and replayability.

Visually, the PC version of Phantom Brave improves upon the original with higher-resolution character models and richer environments, while preserving the game’s distinctive, charming art style. The expressive character designs and colorful, imaginative locales create a world that is both enchanting and inviting. The soundtrack, composed by Tenpei Sato, is another highlight, featuring memorable and emotive themes that enhance both combat intensity and narrative moments. Limited but well-executed voice acting adds personality to key characters and complements the game’s whimsical tone, further drawing players into the world.

While Phantom Brave PC has many strengths, it is not without minor drawbacks. Some players may find the lack of an autosave function frustrating, particularly during longer sessions or challenging battles, as progress can be lost if the game closes unexpectedly. Additionally, certain battles and story segments can feel slow or drawn out, which may test the patience of players seeking a faster-paced tactical experience. Despite these issues, the depth, creativity, and charm of the game more than compensate, making it a rewarding experience for those willing to engage with its mechanics.

Overall, Phantom Brave PC is a distinctive and memorable entry in the tactical RPG genre. Its innovative combat system, heartfelt story, and rich character customization set it apart from more conventional strategy games, while its upgraded visuals and soundtrack enhance the classic experience for modern players. The game’s combination of strategy, whimsy, and emotional storytelling makes it a must-play for fans of tactical RPGs and those looking for a unique, character-driven adventure that rewards thoughtful planning and creative problem-solving.

If you want to try one of the NIS SRPGs other than Disgaea, either play this or Soul Nomad. Maybe La Pucelle as well, although that's a harder recommend. 

I actually did not like this game at first. It did not make a good first impression for me, and I dropped it, only to come back to it a few years later. Most of my playtime has since been on the Switch version, which I recommend over this one, same as with every other NIS SRPG. I'll get into some of the problems I had with the game at first later.

Phantom Brave is certainly a unique SRPG, even compared to the other NIS games. The game it's most similar to is Makai Kingdom, but it doesn't actually play much like Makai Kingdom other than superficial similarities like both being gridless turn based games. The general gameplay involves Marona summoning phantoms by confining them into objects. The phantoms last a few turns before disappearing, which means Marona is the only player character who doesn't have a turn limit. Phantoms are effectively player units, spread into different classes whose stats are further modified by the object you confine them to. This, combined with the gridless gameplay, leads to a lot of strategic implications the player needs to consider. On top of that, everything can be used as a weapon. This includes the objects you can confine phantoms to, as well as the phantoms themselves if they are unarmed. Nothing stops you from using a crate as a weapon, or grabbing an enemy and using them to hit another enemy. 

That said... There are downsides to this system. Since every item is usable as a weapon, every character can only have one item equipped. There is no equipable armor in this game, nor are there consumable items. You also sometimes take home a confined item if a phantom runs out of turns, which means you'll have to go through your inventory to occasionally prune out unwanted items before you hit the rather low inventory cap. 

Phantom Brave did start a few trends that spread to a few other NIS games. For example, all the "out of battle" utility services such as shops and healing are actually done by the same phantoms you can use, and their skills with these services improve as they level. So you might want to actually level up your blacksmith, merchant, fusionist, etc even if you have better units. Phantom Brave is also the first game to feature the Saber Kitty/Slumber cat/Deathsaber monster which inexplicably appears in almost every NIS game after this came out, including the re-release of Disgaea 2.

This is a pretty cool game, but there's some issues with it. Every one of the main stats is occasionally used to calculate damage for certain attacks, which sounds neat at first as you can have high defense characters use their defense stat to attack when equipped with rocks. However since the speed stat also dictates how quick your next turn is, having that stat high and using attacks based on that stat is vastly better than trying to raise both speed and another stat to use to attack. There's also the issue in that there's surprisingly no "ranged" weapons in this game, in spite of the fact that the Archer class from Disgaea is here. There's no bow, no gun, and even spells have fairly low range limits compared to other NIS games. There's also the same high level issue every NIS game before Disgaea 5 has, in that damage calculations tend to result in defensive stats not being able to keep up, making high level combat a oneshotfest. Granted you WANT combat in Phantom Brave to be quick due to the turn limit on phantoms, so it's not as big of a deal in this game.

Anyway, problems aside, this is a cool game. It's the only non-Disgaea NIS SRPG I'd consider better than some of the Disgaea games. There's a bunch of tinkering mechanics to it such as "titles" which give stat boosts to items, characters and dungeons. There's fusion, which lets you combine 2 characters/items to adjust their stats. 

Looking forward to getting the sequel on Switch soon.

Phantom Brave é um jogo interessante:
sendo lançado pouco depois de Disgaea Hour of Darkness o jogo consegue ter alguns autos e baixos, o sistema de batalha é algo bem diferente neste jogo, com uma movimentação que não é baseada em grade, algo que não é normal em um RPG Tático, isso faz o jogo ser mais interessante e traz uma experiencia bem única e divertida para alguém que joga muito esse
tipo de RPG, agora eu gostaria de falar de certos tópicos desse jogo.

HISTÓRIA: a história de phantom brave é um dos fortes desse jogo por um motivo, normalmente na série Disgaea nós controlamos um demônio que já tem uma certa força que vai sendo aprimorada durante a jogatina e a progressão da história, mas no Phantom Brave a protagonista (Marona) é uma pessoa como nós, a únicas grandes especialidades que ela têm é a capacidade de ver e se comunicar com fantasmas junto com o poder de invocar fantasmas temporariamente,
pela marona ter esse poderes ela é mal vista pelas pessoas ao redor dela, isso faz a pessoa a menosprezar mas isso não a
afeta diretamente, em resumo a história de Phantom Brave é sobre preconceito, como ajudar o outro pode mudar a vida
de uma pessoa e se você tiver persistência em algo você alcançar os seus objetivos.
Uma História dessas não muito original mas o que faz ela ser boa é o como ela pode ser bem mais relacionável que uma história de disgaea, junto com os outros personagens que têm suas histórias contadas durante sua jornada com a protagonista.

MÚSICA: A Música é um grande aspecto desse jogo, tendo a maior parte delas sendo intrumental as músicas são muito boas, tendo faixas para cada local novo que você explora combinando bem com o local, as músicas especias com vocal também são muito boas e as versões arranjadas ótimas.

CONTÚDO: A versão de pc traiz o todo o conteúdo acumulado que jogo teve durantes os anos sendo o 3º port do mesmo, a história extra feita para o wii e os personagens especiais do psp estão aqui fazendo esta versão e as lançadas depois desta as verções definitivas de jogar Phantom Brave, com conteúdo que permite você ficar um bom tempo jogando.

Eu recomendo esse jogo caso você tenha muito tempo livre ou tenha um tempo sobrando e quer ter uma experiencia boa com uma história simples mas boa personage interessantes música ótima e gráficos charmosos.

To me Phantom Brave is much more fun than the Disgaea games because it hase more interessting game mechanics. I will list some of the things that made this game addicting to me: 

1. The battle System: 
A) Your phantoms have to be bound to some objects or items on the map. This is an interessting strategic element. If you have no objects near you, you cant summon anything, leaving you unable to fight. So you need to pay attention to your surroundings and make shure you dont run out of objects. You can pick up objects and throw them. So if there is space where you need to summon a phantom, but there is nothing close, you can move something there. 
This gameplay element alone gives this game a very unique touth. And is a major advantage it has over the disgaea games. 
B) Summon round limit: the Phantoms you summon have a time limit, how long they can stay on the battle field. This is also an interessting strategic element. You cant just over level your strongest character and than wreck havoc with it and just kill all enemies on your map with your mean character. Because even Ash your strongest phantom will disappear after a few turns. So you need to deside will you sent him out right away or keep him back, so you can use his strength at the endboss of the map. This gameplay element forces you to build up a team and think about the roles your characters play in the party. Having more strong characters is needed so you can switch someone in after a fighter leaves the map. 

2. Doungeon creation: you can create your own doungeons. They are random generated. But you do see the specifics befor hand and you can choose which doungeon you want to create. This makes doungeons a lot of customise able.

First, when you restart, your character keeps their strength but story enemies reset to low levels, which makes training feel pointless — there’s no reason to reach level 1000 if the strongest story enemies are only level 100. Second, the story maps are amazing, but the generated dungeons are extremely repetitive, and you end up spending more time there than in the actual story. Third, enemies have no way to react if your speed is extremely high, which breaks the balance. These issues greatly reduce the game’s replay value and overall lifespan.

あまりキャラ描写は多くないがそれでもキャラの性格が分かる辺り奇麗にまとめていると思う。
序盤は少し嫌な展開が続くが徐々に評価されていくのを見ることが出来るが、その辺りも割とあっさり書いている

そしてゲーム内容は日本一ソフトらしくクリア後のやりこみ要素であるEXステージやひたすらのキャラの強化。
この部分がゲームの多くの内容を締める。ゲームクリア自体はレベル100前後で出来るがこの後レベル500，1000～など果てのない強化が続く。
このいつものやりこみ要素が好きかどうかがかなり大事。
飽きが来る人もいると多いと思うので、あっさりストーリーで終わるかやり込みまでやるかは決めておいた方が良い。

ゲームとしては普通にまとまっているのでどっちのプレイスタイルでもそれなりに楽しめるゲーム
